# test_camel_to_snake.py

import pytest

# Replace `your_module` with the module where camel_to_snake is defined
from your_module import camel_to_snake


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("input_value", "expected"),
    [
        # Happy path
        ("camelCase", "camel_case"),
        ("helloWorld", "hello_world"),
        ("someLongVariableName", "some_long_variable_name"),

        # Already lowercase / snake case
        ("lowercase", "lowercase"),
        ("already_snake", "already_snake"),

        # PascalCase
        ("CamelCase", "camel_case"),
        ("MyClassName", "my_class_name"),

        # Acronyms / consecutive capitals
        ("HTTPServer", "httpserver"),
        ("myHTTPServer", "my_httpserver"),
        ("XMLHttpRequest", "xmlhttp_request"),

        # Numbers
        ("version2Number", "version2number"),
        ("versionNumber2", "version_number2"),
        ("version2ID", "version2id"),

        # Empty and short strings
        ("", ""),
        ("a", "a"),
        ("A", "a"),

        # Strings with spaces / punctuation
        ("hello World", "hello world"),
        ("hello-World", "hello-world"),
        ("hello.World", "hello.world"),

        # Unicode characters are not matched by [a-z]/[A-Z]
        ("caféMug", "cafémug"),
        ("cafeMug", "cafe_mug"),
    ],
)
def test_camel_to_snake(input_value, expected):
    assert camel_to_snake(input_value) == expected


@pytest.mark.parametrize("invalid_input", [None, 123, 12.5, [], {}, object()])
def test_camel_to_snake_invalid_input_raises_type_error(invalid_input):
    with pytest.raises(TypeError):
        camel_to_snake(invalid_input)
